payload.feature:
Answer the review findings on decision 0046's enactment slice (i), which is committed as 78e33d9 on this branch.

The slice is built and its gates pass: `cargo test --workspace` green, both bundles compile, exact coverage met, the eight delta specs archived under `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i/`, and its `completion.md` records what was done and what the operator still owes. Read that completion note, `docs/decisions/0046-the-boundary-is-named.md` with its addendum, and the archived proposal and design, before you touch anything.

A review of 78e33d9 reached a verdict the engine never received, because the reviewing seat had no write access to its own result path. The verdict was `security-hold`, `max_residual_severity: high`, `has_security_residual: true`, and its findings are reproduced here verbatim in substance. Answer the first three. Do not answer the last two.

1. **HIGH, security — path normalization collapses two different filenames.** `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs` around line 3302 normalizes such that the Unix filename `scripts/gate.sh` and the literal single-file name `scripts\gate.sh` collapse to the same key, while the original bytes are kept for the latter. A repository can therefore carry a file whose real name contains a backslash, have it collapse onto the pinned key of a different file, and conceal changes to the script that actually executes — bypassing the unboxed spawn re-walk with no race required. Fix it so a pinned script's identity is the bytes of its real name, and pin the case in a test that plants both names in one layer.

2. **MEDIUM, correctness — whole-layer revalidation rejects the engine's own writes.** `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs` around line 2322 re-walks the whole layer, which for a realm scaffolded by `brokkr init .` includes the journal, `.forge/results/` and the implementation's own edits, so an unboxed gate in that realm rejects changes the engine itself made during the run. The existing tests miss it because they use a separate bundle directory. Narrow the re-walk to what the pin actually covers, and pin the `init .` shape in a test.

3. **LOW, simplicity — redundant fragment removal.** `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs` around line 3715 removes a fragment that unboxed resolution already omits. Delete the redundant step or explain in a comment why it is not redundant.

Do NOT act on these two, which the operator accepted as residuals in D34 and which Muninn patrols; the reviewer named them as accepted and so do you:
- the delivery summary omitting the absence warning when both manifest keys exist and no boundary entry does;
- the gate-law delta lacking an explicit open-work scenario.

Constraints, unchanged and binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin every witness and compose digest that moves from the tests' own left/right pairs. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Path comparisons stay canonical-safe and platform-neutral. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Commit on this branch. Claude's `hands.harness` fragments and codex's capture measurement remain the operator's and stay in their recorded deferred state.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.
